title: Install GitTree on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)
promise: Install the universal GitTree disk image on a Mac and get past the first-launch warning.
concept: GitTree is a front end for the Git already on your computer, so Git must be installed first.

title: Install GitTree on Windows 10 and 11
promise: Run the GitTree setup on Windows and get past the SmartScreen warning.
concept: GitTree uses Git for Windows as its Git, and needs version 2.39 or newer.

title: Install GitTree on Ubuntu and Debian (.deb)
promise: Install the .deb package with apt and start GitTree from the menu.
concept: apt resolves dependencies for a local package, and GitTree needs Git 2.39 or newer.

title: Run GitTree on Linux with the AppImage (no root)
promise: Make the AppImage executable and run GitTree without installing anything.
concept: A portable AppImage runs from any folder and does not register the opengittree:// link handler.

title: Verify a GitTree Linux download with SHA256SUMS
promise: Check that a downloaded installer matches the checksum published with the release.
concept: A checksum catches a corrupt download but not a compromised release.

title: Which Git version does GitTree need? (2.39 or newer)
promise: Check your Git version and read the two screens GitTree shows when Git is missing or too old.
concept: GitTree never bundles Git: it runs the git command you already have.

title: Sign in to GitTree on first launch (website account)
promise: Sign in through the GitTree website from the app, including the manual code fallback.
concept: Your GitTree account (website) is separate from your Git identity and your hosting accounts.

title: Open a Git repository in GitTree (folder or drag and drop)
promise: Open an existing repository from the New Tab page, the Open shortcut or a dropped folder.
concept: A repository is a working folder plus a .git directory.

title: Trust this repository? What GitTree checks before it opens
promise: Read the trust prompt and choose between Restricted Mode and Trust and Open.
concept: A cloned repository's config and hooks can run programs on your machine.

title: Clone a Git repository by URL in GitTree
promise: Clone a repository from a URL into a folder you choose and open it.
concept: A clone copies the full history and sets the remote named origin.

title: Create a new Git repository in GitTree (git init)
promise: Initialise a new repository with a first branch name and an optional .gitignore template and licence.
concept: git init creates the object database and the first branch.

title: Recent repositories and the New Tab page in GitTree
promise: Reopen a repository from the Recent list and remove one from it without deleting files.
concept: The recent list is stored by the app, nothing in the repository changes.

title: GitTree window tour: sidebar, graph, inspector, drawer
promise: Learn where the four areas of the window are and how to toggle each one.
concept: The window is a view over one repository: refs on the left, history in the centre, details on the right.

title: What is a Git commit? See one in GitTree
promise: See that a commit is a snapshot with a parent, a message and an author, using the Commit Details panel.
concept: A commit is a snapshot (tree) plus parents, message, author and committer.

title: The Git commit graph explained: history is a DAG
promise: Read the commit graph: parents, lanes and why history is a graph and not a line.
concept: History is a directed acyclic graph in which lanes show parallel lines of work.

title: Git branches are just pointers (refs explained)
promise: See branch pills on the graph and learn that a ref is a movable name for a commit.
concept: A ref (branch name) is a movable pointer to a commit.

title: What is HEAD in Git? Find it in GitTree
promise: Jump to HEAD and see what the checked-out branch and a detached HEAD look like.
concept: HEAD is the current commit, usually through the checked-out branch.

title: Git working tree, index and HEAD: the three trees
promise: Use the Working Changes panel to see the working folder, the index and HEAD as three different states.
concept: Git compares three trees: the working tree, the index (staging area) and HEAD.

title: Local vs remote branches in Git (origin/main explained)
promise: Read the left panel and the ahead and behind counts to tell local branches from remote-tracking ones.
concept: A remote-tracking branch is your local record of where the remote's branch was at the last fetch.

title: What is a Git remote? Add, edit and remove one
promise: Add, edit and remove a remote and see that it is only a name for a URL.
concept: A remote is a named URL (with an optional separate push URL).

title: Git tags explained: create a tag in GitTree
promise: Create a lightweight tag on a commit and see it as a pill in the graph.
concept: A lightweight tag is a fixed name on a commit.

title: Git fetch explained: download without changing your files
promise: Run Fetch All and watch only the remote-tracking branches move while your files stay put.
concept: Fetch updates remote-tracking refs and never touches your working files or your branches.

title: What is a Git fast-forward? Move a branch pointer
promise: Fast-forward a branch to its upstream and see that only the pointer moves.
concept: A fast-forward moves a branch pointer along a straight line and creates no commit.

title: Git merge vs rebase: the difference on the graph
promise: Drag one branch onto another and compare what Merge and Rebase do to the graph.
concept: Merge joins two lines of history with a new commit; rebase replays commits with new ids.

title: Git config scopes: system, global and local explained
promise: Change a Git setting at the global and the local level from Preferences and see which one wins.
concept: Git settings live in scopes (system, global, local) and the narrowest scope wins.

title: Stage a file in GitTree (git add explained)
promise: Stage one changed file so that it goes into the next commit and the others do not.
concept: Staging copies a file's changes into the index, which is the next commit.

title: Stage a single hunk in GitTree (commit part of a file)
promise: Commit only one of two changes in the same file, without touching the other.
concept: The staging area (index) decides what a commit contains; a hunk is the unit of a change.

title: Stage single lines in GitTree (partial commit)
promise: Pick individual changed lines and stage only those.
concept: A patch can be narrowed to single lines before it enters the index.
commands: git add -p (then e to edit the hunk)

title: Unstage a file in GitTree (undo git add)
promise: Move a staged file back to the unstaged list without losing any edit.
concept: Unstaging resets the index entry and leaves the file on disk untouched.

title: Make a Git commit in GitTree step by step
promise: Write a summary and description and commit the staged changes.
concept: A commit snapshots the index, not the working folder.

title: Write better Git commit messages with GitTree hints
promise: Use the summary counter and the message hints, including the Conventional Commits check.
concept: A commit message has a short summary, a blank line, then an optional body.

title: Amend the last Git commit in GitTree
promise: Fix the message or add a forgotten file to the last commit.
concept: Amend replaces the tip commit with a new one that has a new id.

title: Git commit options: sign-off, skip hooks, other author
promise: Open the Commit Options menu and use sign-off, a different author and recent messages.
concept: A commit records an author and a committer separately, and can carry a sign-off trailer.

title: Add co-authors to a Git commit in GitTree
promise: Credit a second person on a commit with a Co-authored-by trailer.
concept: A trailer is a key and value line at the end of a commit message.

title: Git commit hooks: read pre-commit output in GitTree
promise: See what a failing pre-commit hook prints and why your message and staged changes are kept.
concept: A hook is a script in .git/hooks that can stop a commit.

title: Draft a Git commit message with your own AI agent CLI
promise: Generate a commit message from the staged diff using a coding-agent CLI you installed and signed in to.
concept: The staged diff is the input to a message, and it is sent only when you click.

title: Discard changes to a file in GitTree (git restore)
promise: Throw away the changes in one file, knowing a recovery snapshot is saved first.
concept: Discarding is irreversible in plain Git, so GitTree snapshots to a private ref before acting.

title: Discard a single hunk in GitTree (undo part of a file)
promise: Throw away one hunk of a file and keep the other.
concept: A hunk can be reverse-applied to the working tree on its own.

title: Discard all changes in a Git repository safely
promise: Reset the whole working folder to the last commit with one confirmed action.
concept: Resetting the tree to HEAD removes both staged and unstaged work.

title: Ignore a file, folder or extension in Git (.gitignore)
promise: Add a path to .gitignore from the right-click menu.
concept: .gitignore tells Git which untracked files to leave out.

title: Edit .gitignore and find out why a file is ignored
promise: Edit .gitignore with a template and ask which rule ignores a given path.
concept: git check-ignore -v names the exact rule and file that ignores a path.

title: Git diff in GitTree: hunk, inline and side by side
promise: Switch the diff between Hunk, Inline and Split views.
concept: A diff is added and removed lines shown with their context.

title: Jump between changes in a Git diff (F7 and Shift+F7)
promise: Move to the next and previous change with the keyboard and the change overview.
concept: Reading a long diff is faster when you jump from change to change.

title: Ignore whitespace in a Git diff and wrap long lines
promise: Turn on Ignore whitespace, Wrap lines and Highlight changed words.
concept: Whitespace-only changes are noise that git diff -w removes.

title: Compare images in Git: side by side, swipe, onion skin
promise: Compare two versions of an image with the three image diff modes.
concept: Git stores binary files as blobs, so GitTree reads both blobs and compares them visually.

title: View a file at any Git commit in GitTree
promise: Open a file as it was at a chosen commit using File View.
concept: Every commit holds a complete snapshot, so any file can be read at any revision.

title: Compare two Git commits in GitTree (git diff A B)
promise: Select two commits and see the files that differ between them.
concept: A diff between two commits compares two snapshots, not two changes.

title: Restore a file from an old Git commit in GitTree
promise: Bring one file back to how it was in a chosen commit.
concept: Restoring overwrites your work, so GitTree saves it in a recovery ref first.

title: Git blame: who changed this line? (GitTree blame view)
promise: Open Blame on a file and see which commit last touched each line.
concept: Blame attributes each line to the commit that last changed it.

title: Git blame before this commit: walk a line's history
promise: Step back to the blame of the commit before the one that changed a line.
concept: Blaming at a commit's parent reveals who changed the line before.

title: Git file history with renames (git log --follow)
promise: List every commit that changed one file, across renames.
concept: File history can follow a file through renames.

title: The WIP row in the Git graph: your uncommitted work
promise: Read the WIP row at the top of the graph and open the working changes from it.
concept: The working tree is the uncommitted tip of your history.

title: Search Git history in GitTree (Ctrl+F in the graph)
promise: Search the loaded history by message, author, SHA, branch or tag and jump between matches.
concept: Searching what is already loaded is instant, and it is limited to the loaded rows.

title: Git stash in GitTree: save work in progress
promise: Stash all your changes to get a clean working folder.
concept: A stash is a pair of commits on refs/stash that holds your uncommitted work.

title: Git stash pop in GitTree: bring your changes back
promise: Pop the latest stash to restore it and remove it from the list.
concept: Pop applies a stash and drops it in one step.

title: Create a Git branch in GitTree
promise: Create a branch at the current commit and check it out.
concept: Creating a branch writes a new pointer to a commit and nothing else.

title: Switch Git branches in GitTree (git switch)
promise: Check out another branch, including what GitTree offers when local changes are in the way.
concept: Checkout moves HEAD, and local changes can block it.

title: Check out a remote Git branch and track it
promise: Check out a remote branch so that a local branch tracks it.
concept: A local branch can track a remote branch (its upstream).

title: Rename a Git branch in GitTree
promise: Rename a local branch and see the pill change.
concept: Renaming moves a pointer's name, not its commits.

title: Delete a Git branch safely in GitTree
promise: Delete a local branch and see that its last commit is kept in a recovery ref.
concept: Deleting a branch removes the pointer; the commits stay reachable until they are cleaned up.

title: Set the upstream branch in Git (tracking explained)
promise: Choose which remote branch a local branch tracks, or make it track nothing.
concept: The upstream is the remote branch that pull, push and ahead and behind counts compare against.

title: Create an annotated Git tag in GitTree
promise: Create an annotated tag with a message for a release.
concept: An annotated tag is its own object with a message, unlike a lightweight tag.

title: Delete a Git tag locally and on the remote
promise: Delete a tag from your repository and, separately, from the remote.
concept: Deleting a remote tag affects everyone who fetches.

title: Preview a Git merge for conflicts before you merge
promise: See whether a merge will conflict, and in which files, before anything changes.
concept: A merge can be predicted without touching your files.

title: Merge a Git branch in GitTree (merge commit)
promise: Merge one branch into the current branch and choose how it is recorded.
concept: A merge commit has two parents; a fast-forward has none to add.

title: Git squash merge: combine a branch into one commit
promise: Squash a branch into the staged changes and commit it as one commit.
concept: A squash merge copies a branch's changes without recording its history.

title: Git merge in progress: the operation banner in GitTree
promise: Read the operation banner and know when to Resolve, Continue, Skip or Abort.
concept: An unfinished operation is recorded in state files inside .git.

title: Abort a Git merge or rebase and go back to before
promise: Abort an operation in one step and see that your work is kept under a recovery ref.
concept: An abort restores the state from before the operation started.

title: Merge conflicts in Git: find the conflicted files
promise: Read the Conflicted Files and Resolved Files lists and mark files resolved.
concept: A conflicted file has three versions in the index: base, ours and theirs.

title: Resolve a Git merge conflict in GitTree's merge view
promise: Resolve one conflict line by line in the three-pane editor and save it as resolved.
concept: Resolving a conflict means choosing the final content, then staging it.

title: Resolve a Git conflict by taking one whole side
promise: Resolve a file by keeping ours or theirs entirely, including delete versus modify.
concept: --ours and --theirs pick a whole version of a conflicted file.

title: Use an external merge tool for Git conflicts
promise: Open a conflicted file in the merge tool you configured and return to GitTree.
concept: A merge tool is a program Git hands the base, local and remote versions to.

title: Git flow in GitTree: initialise the branching model
promise: Initialise Gitflow with your production and development branches and prefixes.
concept: Gitflow is a naming and merging convention built on ordinary branches and merges.

title: Git flow: start and finish a feature branch
promise: Start a feature, commit on it, and finish it back into develop.
concept: Finishing a Gitflow feature is a no-fast-forward merge followed by deleting the branch.

title: Predict Git merge conflicts before they happen
promise: Read the early conflict warning chip on a branch and the setting that controls it.
concept: Git can compute a merge result in memory without changing any file.

title: Git rebase explained: rebase a branch in GitTree
promise: Rebase the current branch onto another and see the commits get new ids.
concept: Rebase replays your commits on a new base, creating new commits.

title: Git interactive rebase in GitTree (pick, squash, drop)
promise: Rearrange, combine and drop commits in the interactive rebase editor.
concept: An interactive rebase is a todo list of actions applied to a range of commits.

title: Change a Git commit message after committing (reword)
promise: Reword an older commit message from the graph.
concept: Changing any commit message gives that commit and every commit above it a new id.

title: Remove a commit from Git history (drop a commit)
promise: Drop a commit from the graph and see how Undo can bring it back.
concept: Dropping a commit removes it from the branch but not from the object database.

title: Reorder Git commits: move a commit up or down
promise: Move a commit up or down in the history from the right-click menu.
concept: Reordering commits replays them in a new order, which can conflict.

title: Squash Git commits into one in GitTree
promise: Select several commits and squash them into one.
concept: Squashing folds the changes of several commits into one commit.

title: Why rewriting pushed Git commits is risky
promise: See the warning GitTree shows when commits you are about to rewrite are already on a remote.
concept: Rewriting shared history forces everyone else to reconcile it.

title: Git cherry-pick: copy a commit to another branch
promise: Copy one commit onto the current branch.
concept: Cherry-pick re-applies a commit's change on top of HEAD as a new commit.

title: Git revert: undo a commit without rewriting history
promise: Revert a commit by adding a new commit that undoes it.
concept: A revert is a new inverse commit, which is safe on shared history.

title: Git reset --soft: undo a commit but keep it staged
promise: Move the branch back one commit while the changes stay staged.
concept: A soft reset moves only the branch pointer.

title: Git reset --mixed: undo a commit, keep the changes
promise: Move the branch back and the index with it, keeping your files.
concept: A mixed reset moves the branch pointer and resets the index.

title: Git reset --hard in GitTree: discard commits safely
promise: Hard-reset a branch and recover the discarded work from the snapshot GitTree takes first.
concept: A hard reset moves the branch, the index and the files, so it can lose work.

title: Undo and redo Git operations in GitTree
promise: Undo a rebase and a branch delete from the toolbar and redo them.
concept: Undo restores a ref from a journal entry, only if the ref has not moved since.

title: Git recovery snapshots: GitTree's refs/ogt/trash
promise: Find the recovery snapshots GitTree keeps and delete the old ones.
concept: A snapshot is a commit kept alive under a private ref so nothing is lost.

title: Git reflog explained: see where HEAD has been
promise: Open the reflog of a branch and read the list of places it pointed to.
concept: The reflog is the local record of where each ref used to point.

title: Recover a lost Git commit with the reflog
promise: Create a branch from a reflog entry to get back a commit that no branch points to.
concept: A commit with no ref is still in the database until garbage collection.

title: Git bisect: find the commit that introduced a bug
promise: Mark commits good and bad until GitTree names the first bad commit.
concept: Bisect is a binary search through history.

title: Create a Git patch file from a commit (format-patch)
promise: Save one or more commits as a patch file you can send.
concept: A patch file is a portable description of a commit.

title: Apply a Git patch file: git apply vs git am
promise: Apply a patch to the working tree, to the index, or as commits.
concept: git apply changes files, while git am also creates the commits.

title: Git push in GitTree: send your commits to a remote
promise: Push a branch, including the first push that picks the remote branch.
concept: A push sends commits and moves a ref on the remote.

title: Check where a Git push will go before you push
promise: Read the destination check and choose a different target if it is wrong.
concept: push.default and push remotes decide where a plain push lands.

title: Git pull --ff-only in GitTree
promise: Pull with fast-forward only and see it refuse when histories have diverged.
concept: Pull is a fetch followed by an integration; fast-forward only refuses when branches diverged.

title: Git pull: fast-forward if possible, else merge
promise: Pull when both sides have new commits and get a merge commit.
concept: Pull in merge mode ties your commits and the remote's with a merge commit.

title: Git pull --rebase in GitTree
promise: Pull by replaying your local commits on top of the remote's.
concept: Pull with rebase keeps a straight history by replaying local commits.

title: Choose your default Git pull mode in GitTree
promise: Set what the toolbar Pull button does: fast-forward only, merge or rebase.
concept: The pull mode is a policy: how your branch takes in the remote's new commits.

title: Git push rejected (non-fast-forward): how to fix it
promise: Understand the refused-push dialog and choose Fetch, Merge and Push or Rebase and Push.
concept: A push is refused when the remote has commits you do not have.

title: Git force push with lease: the safe way in GitTree
promise: Force-push a rewritten branch so that it refuses if the remote moved.
concept: --force-with-lease overwrites the remote only if it still has the commit you last saw.

title: Delete a remote Git branch from GitTree
promise: Delete a branch on the remote without leaving GitTree.
concept: Deleting a remote branch pushes a deletion to the server.

title: Push a Git tag to the remote in GitTree
promise: Push a single tag to the remote.
concept: Tags are not pushed with a branch unless you ask for them.

title: Git auto-fetch: keep remote branches up to date
promise: Turn on auto-fetch with an interval and see why it never asks for credentials.
concept: A background fetch updates remote-tracking refs and never changes your files.

title: Connect GitHub to GitTree (browser sign-in or token)
promise: Connect a GitHub account with the browser device code or a personal access token.
concept: A hosting account lets the app talk to the host's API; the Git commands still use your credentials.

title: Connect GitHub Enterprise Server to GitTree
promise: Name your Enterprise Server host and connect with a token or browser sign-in.
concept: A self-hosted host needs its own address and its own application ID.

title: Connect GitLab to GitTree (token or application ID)
promise: Connect gitlab.com or a self-managed GitLab with a token or a typed OAuth application ID.
concept: Not every host offers one-click browser sign-in, so a personal access token is the fallback.

title: Connect Bitbucket Cloud to GitTree
promise: Connect Bitbucket Cloud with browser sign-in, an API token or an access token.
concept: Some hosts sign you in through an authorization code and an account service.

title: Connect Azure DevOps to GitTree (personal access token)
promise: Connect Azure DevOps with a personal access token.
concept: A personal access token is a password scoped to what you allow.

title: Connect Bitbucket Data Center to GitTree
promise: Connect a Bitbucket Data Center host through your administrator's OAuth application link.
concept: A self-hosted server needs an administrator-created application link before browser sign-in works.

title: Clone a repository from your hosting account in GitTree
promise: Browse the repositories of a connected account and clone one.
concept: The account only lists repositories; the clone itself is plain git over HTTPS.

title: Publish a local Git repository to a host from GitTree
promise: Create the repository on your host, add it as origin and push, in one dialog.
concept: Publishing is three steps in one: create the remote repository, add origin, push.

title: Create a pull request from GitTree
promise: Push a branch and start a pull request with a title and description, as a draft if you like.
concept: A pull request is a host feature that proposes merging one branch into another.

title: Check out a pull request branch locally in GitTree
promise: Fetch a pull request head and check out its branch.
concept: A host publishes each pull request head as a ref you can fetch.

title: Review pull request files and diffs in GitTree
promise: Read the changed files of a pull request.
concept: A pull request diff is the difference between the branch and its merge base.

title: Comment on and resolve pull request threads in GitTree
promise: Post a comment, reply to a thread and resolve it.
concept: Review comments belong to lines and threads, and a thread can be resolved.

title: See pull request checks and re-run them in GitTree
promise: Read the checks of a pull request and re-run a failed one.
concept: Checks are automated results the host attaches to a commit.

title: Review a pull request: approve or request changes
promise: Submit a review on a pull request and edit its details.
concept: A review is a verdict plus comments from a person other than the author.

title: Merge a pull request: merge, squash or rebase
promise: Merge a pull request on the host with the method you choose.
concept: The host merges server-side, guarded by the expected head commit.

title: See issues and start a branch from one in GitTree
promise: Open an issue from the sidebar and create a branch for it.
concept: An issue is a host record; the branch is plain Git.

title: Create an issue from GitTree
promise: Create a new issue with a title and a Markdown description.
concept: Creating an issue is a call to the host's API, not a Git operation.

title: Git fork workflow: add a remote from a fork in GitTree
promise: Add a remote that points to someone's fork over HTTPS or SSH.
concept: A fork workflow uses several remotes, typically origin and upstream.

title: Git worktrees explained: see them in GitTree
promise: Find the Worktrees section and understand what several working folders share.
concept: A worktree is another working folder that shares the same object database.

title: Create a Git worktree in GitTree (git worktree add)
promise: Create a worktree for a branch or a new branch in a separate folder.
concept: A branch can be checked out in only one worktree at a time.

title: Move, lock and remove a Git worktree
promise: Move, lock, remove and prune worktrees safely.
concept: Git tracks worktrees in the main repository, so moving one by hand breaks the link.

title: Git submodules explained: see them in GitTree
promise: Read the Submodules section and its states.
concept: A submodule pins another repository at one exact commit.

title: Add a Git submodule in GitTree
promise: Add a submodule at a path, optionally following a branch.
concept: Adding a submodule records a .gitmodules entry and a pinned commit.

title: Update and remove a Git submodule in GitTree
promise: Initialise, update, sync and remove a submodule.
concept: Updating a submodule checks out the commit the parent repository records.

title: Set up Git LFS for a repository in GitTree
promise: Check that Git LFS is installed and set it up for this repository.
concept: Large files live outside the repository and pointer files live inside.

title: Track large files with Git LFS in GitTree
promise: Track and untrack a file pattern with LFS.
concept: Tracking writes a pattern into .gitattributes.

title: Download and prune Git LFS content in GitTree
promise: Download LFS file content and prune old content.
concept: An LFS pointer is replaced by the real file only when the content is downloaded.

title: Git LFS file locking in GitTree
promise: Lock and unlock a lockable file and see who holds a lock.
concept: A lock stops others editing a binary file that cannot be merged.

title: Git sparse checkout in GitTree: only the folders you need
promise: Check out only chosen folders of a large repository, and bring everything back later.
concept: Cone-mode sparse checkout limits the working tree to selected directories.

title: Shallow, sparse and blobless Git clones in GitTree
promise: Clone a big repository faster with depth, sparse or blobless options, and fetch more history later.
concept: Shallow, partial and sparse clones trade completeness for speed.

title: Git stash options: untracked files, staged only, message
promise: Stash with a message, include untracked files or stash only the staged changes.
concept: git stash push can limit what it saves and what it leaves behind.

title: Create a Git branch from a stash in GitTree
promise: Turn an old stash into a branch.
concept: A stash is a commit, so it can become a branch.

title: Delete a Git stash and recover it from the snapshots
promise: Delete a stash and see that it is kept in the recovery snapshots.
concept: Dropping a stash normally loses its commit, so GitTree keeps a recovery ref.

title: Git repository maintenance in GitTree (fsck, gc)
promise: Check integrity, speed up history and clean up the object database.
concept: Git needs occasional housekeeping of its object database.

title: Group repositories into workspaces in GitTree
promise: Create a workspace, add repositories to it and open them all.
concept: A workspace is an app-level grouping; it is not a Git feature.

title: Work in several repositories with tabs in GitTree
promise: Open, switch, reorder and close repository tabs.
concept: Each tab is an independent session of one repository.

title: The GitTree command palette: run anything from the keyboard
promise: Open the palette and run commands, jump to refs and switch repositories with the prefixes.
concept: One searchable list replaces menus for commands, refs and repositories.

title: Search all Git history by message, author, file or change
promise: Search every commit with the # mode and the author, file and change filters.
concept: git log can search all of history without loading it into the graph.

title: Find any file fast in GitTree (fuzzy file finder)
promise: Find a file with the : mode and open its history.
concept: git ls-files lists tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored paths.

title: The integrated terminal in GitTree
promise: Open a terminal in the repository folder, add more terminals and rename them.
concept: The terminal is a real shell opened at the repository root.

title: Define custom commands in GitTree (programs with tokens)
promise: Add a custom command that runs a program with the repository, branch, SHA or file as arguments.
concept: A custom command is a program plus arguments, with no shell involved.

title: Run a custom command from the GitTree toolbar
promise: Run a saved custom command and read its confirmation and output.
concept: Running arbitrary programs needs an explicit confirmation.

title: Filter the Git graph by author, date, branch or path
promise: Show only the commits that match a filter and clear it again.
concept: git log can restrict history by author, dates and paths over chosen starting points.

title: See all your pull requests across a workspace
promise: Use the Pull requests tab of the Workspaces page to see what needs your review.
concept: A dashboard is a view over the host's API across many repositories.

title: GitTree Preferences: search, scopes and reset
promise: Find a setting with search, see where it is saved, and reset it.
concept: Every setting has an origin: built-in default, app, profile, repository or Git config.

title: Change the GitTree theme: dark, light, high contrast
promise: Choose a theme, or follow the system appearance.
concept: Themes only change colours, never Git data.

title: Zoom, date format and reduced motion in GitTree
promise: Zoom the interface, choose a date format and show or hide sidebar sections.
concept: Display preferences change how the same history is shown.

title: Git profiles in GitTree: work and personal identities
promise: Create two profiles with different names and emails and switch between them.
concept: user.name and user.email decide who a commit says it is from.

title: SSH keys in GitTree: generate, copy and test
promise: Generate an Ed25519 key, copy its public half and test a connection.
concept: An SSH key pair proves who you are without a password.

title: SSH host key and username prompts in GitTree
promise: Answer the 'Connect to host?' prompt safely and choose how unknown host keys are treated.
concept: The first SSH connection to a server asks you to trust its host key.

title: Sign Git commits in GitTree (OpenPGP, SSH, S/MIME)
promise: Choose a signing key and turn on signing for every commit.
concept: A signed commit proves who created it.

title: Set an external diff tool, merge tool and editor
promise: Pick the diff tool, merge tool and editor GitTree opens for you.
concept: Diff and merge tools are programs Git hands file versions to.

title: GitTree keyboard shortcuts: the cheat sheet
promise: Open the Keyboard Shortcuts sheet and find the shortcut for any command.
concept: Shortcuts are bindings from key chords to command ids.

title: Customise keyboard shortcuts in GitTree
promise: Change, remove and reset a shortcut and see how conflicts are reported.
concept: Two commands cannot share one chord in the same context.

title: See the exact Git commands GitTree runs (Activity Log)
promise: Open the Activity Log to read each git command, its output and its result.
concept: Everything the app does is a plain git command you can read and repeat.

title: Report a bug or a crash from GitTree
promise: Open Crash Reports, copy the text and report it on GitHub.
concept: A useful bug report names the version, the steps and the log, with no secrets.

title: Update GitTree: check for updates, download and install
promise: Check for an update, see the download get verified and restart to install it.
concept: The app verifies a download by SHA-256 against the published release.

title: GitTree startup screens: update, offline, maintenance
promise: Understand each startup gate screen and what to do on each, including the 7-day offline grace.
concept: The official build checks a release gate at launch and works offline for a limited time.

title: Sign out of GitTree everywhere
promise: Sign out of your GitTree account and see that connected hosting accounts stay connected.
concept: Your GitTree account and your hosting accounts are separate.

title: Restricted mode in GitTree: open untrusted repos safely
promise: Work in Restricted Mode and review the trust decision later.
concept: An untrusted repository's configuration and hooks must not run.

title: Where GitTree stores your tokens (system keychain)
promise: See that tokens go to the system keychain and how to disconnect an account or forget all credentials.
concept: Credentials belong in the operating system's secure store, never in a file or a URL.

title: Linux keyring for GitTree: Secret Service setup
promise: Make sure a Secret Service (GNOME Keyring or KeePassXC) is running so GitTree can save tokens.
concept: On Linux the freedesktop Secret Service is the system keychain.

title: Import a custom theme into GitTree
promise: Import a theme file and use it next to the built-in themes.
concept: A theme is data that GitTree reads, not code it runs.

title: Export, import and reset GitTree settings
promise: Export your settings, import them on another computer and reset everything if needed.
concept: Settings are portable data; some Git settings write to your global config only after you confirm.
